title: Sorting and Filtering Orders in DB Browser for SQLite
description: A short, hands-on course for beginners that builds core data-analysis skills—browsing, sorting, and filtering—using a single e-commerce orders dataset in DB Browser for SQLite.
target_audience: Beginner data analysts with no SQL experience

videos.title: Browsing the Orders Table
videos.learning_objective: Understand how a table organizes data into rows and columns before any manipulation is applied.
videos.discovery_objective: Open the Browse Data tab and display the Orders table with all 500 rows and 6 columns (order_id, customer_name, region, order_date, amount, status) visible.

exercise_artifact.description: A single Orders table representing customer purchases used consistently throughout the course.

videos.new_capability: Opening and viewing a raw table in Browse Data
videos.running_example_usage: The learner opens the Orders table for the first time to see its full structure.
videos.preview_text_hint: Next we'll sort the Orders table by amount to see the smallest and largest orders.

videos.title: Sorting by One Column
videos.learning_objective: Understand how clicking a column header reorders rows by that column's value.
videos.discovery_objective: Click the amount column header in the Orders table within the Browse Data tab so rows display in ascending order with $4.99 as the top value.

exercise_artifact.description: A single Orders table representing customer purchases used consistently throughout the course.

videos.new_capability: Sorting a single column by clicking its header
videos.running_example_usage: The learner sorts the same Orders table by the amount column to find the cheapest order.
videos.proof_numbers: Lowest amount after sorting: $4.99; total rows unchanged at 500.
videos.recap_text_hint: In the last video we opened the Orders table and saw all 500 rows with 6 columns including order_id, amount, and status.
videos.preview_text_hint: Next we'll filter the Orders table to show only rows where status equals 'Shipped'.

videos.title: Filtering by an Exact Match
videos.learning_objective: Understand how typing a value into a column's filter box narrows visible rows to an exact match.
videos.discovery_objective: Type Shipped into the filter box under the status column in the Orders table within the Browse Data tab so only matching rows remain visible.

exercise_artifact.description: A single Orders table representing customer purchases used consistently throughout the course.

videos.new_capability: Filtering rows by exact text match using a column filter box
videos.running_example_usage: The learner filters the Orders table to isolate only shipped orders.
videos.proof_numbers: 210 of 500 rows remain visible after filtering status = 'Shipped'.
videos.recap_text_hint: In the last video we sorted the Orders table by amount and saw $4.99 as the smallest value.
videos.preview_text_hint: Next we'll filter the Orders table using a comparison so only high-value orders remain.

videos.title: Filtering with a Comparison Operator
videos.learning_objective: Understand how a comparison expression in a filter box narrows rows by a numeric threshold rather than an exact match.
videos.discovery_objective: Type >200 into the filter box under the amount column in the Orders table within the Browse Data tab so only rows with amount greater than 200 remain visible.

exercise_artifact.description: A single Orders table representing customer purchases used consistently throughout the course.

videos.new_capability: Filtering numeric rows using a comparison operator
videos.running_example_usage: The learner filters the same Orders table to reveal only high-value orders above $200.
videos.proof_numbers: 85 of 500 rows remain visible after filtering amount > 200.
videos.recap_text_hint: In the last video we filtered the Orders table to show only the 210 rows where status equals 'Shipped'.

running_example.name: E-commerce Orders
running_example.description: A single Orders table representing customer purchases used consistently throughout the course.
